_schema.note: Each entry describes one published saint page. feast_day is MM-DD in the primary tradition given (default: Catholic Church, Roman Rite, Ordinary Form unless noted). If a saint has multiple widely-recognized feast dates across traditions, list them in feast_days_other so the homepage can still surface the page on those days too.

fields.slug: lowercase-hyphenated id, matches saints/st-[slug].html and saints/previews/st-[slug].png
fields.name: full display name as it appears on the page
fields.tagline: the one-line thesis from the page hero
fields.feast_day_tradition: which calendar the primary date follows, e.g. 'Catholic Church (Roman Rite)'
fields.feast_days_other: array of {tradition, date, date_display} for other denominations, optional
fields.patronage: short patronage string for the fact chip
fields.era: short era string for the fact chip, e.g. '1st century'
fields.page: relative path to the HTML page
fields.added: YYYY-MM-DD this entry was added to the manifest
fields.release_date: OPTIONAL. YYYY-MM-DD (full date, not MM-DD). The saint stays completely invisible on the site -- no hero, no week strip, no archive card -- until local midnight of this date, then appears automatically and stays visible from then on. This is what lets you bulk-add many saints at once and have them post themselves on their assigned day. Falls back to `added` if omitted, so old entries without this field keep working unchanged. Note this is a one-time real-world release gate, separate from `feast_day` (which is the recurring MM-DD used every year for the homepage's 'feast day today' match).

saints.name: St. Lydia of Thyatira
saints.tagline: The purple-dye merchant whose opened heart opened the first door of the Church in Europe
saints.feast_day_tradition: Catholic Church (Extraordinary Form) / widely cited general Catholic date

saints.name: St. Oswald of Northumbria
saints.tagline: The warrior king who planted a cross before the battle that brought Christianity back to Northumbria

saints.name: St. John Vianney
saints.tagline: The parish priest who turned a forgotten village into the great hospital of souls, one confession at a time
saints.feast_day_tradition: Catholic Church (current Roman Calendar) / Church of England

saints.name: St. Sixtus II
saints.tagline: Arrested mid-Mass in a Roman catacomb and beheaded within the hour — his name has been spoken at the altar at every Mass since

saints.name: St. Dominic
saints.tagline: He chose poverty and persuasion over the crusade being fought around him, and founded a preaching order that would outlive every army sent to do what he refused to

saints.name: St. Teresa Benedicta of the Cross
saints.tagline: A Jewish philosopher who lost her faith, found it again through a book read in one night, became a Carmelite nun, and died at Auschwitz for who she was and who she had become
saints.feast_day_tradition: Catholic Church (current General Roman Calendar, optional memorial)

saints.name: St. Lawrence
saints.tagline: Ordered to hand over the Church's wealth, he spent three days distributing it to the poor, then presented the poor themselves as the treasure — and was executed for the joke
saints.feast_day_tradition: Catholic Church, Anglican Communion & Lutheran churches
saints.patronage: The poor, cooks, deacons, firefighters, comedians
